subject: general
question: Which form of carbon is used as a dry lubricant?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Graphite**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **allotrope of carbon**, **graphite** is used as a dry lubricant.
 
• **Graphite** is** slippery in nature** and offers lubrication at **high temperatures**. It is, thus, used as a **dry lubricant** and is mostly preferred better than liquid and oil lubricants.
 
• Graphite as a **dry lubricant** has **applications **in the food industry,** air compressors**, machine shop works, **lubricating locks**, piano actions, **ball bearings, open gears**, brass instrument valves, etc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **atoms of diamond are grouped in a crystal structure **known as **diamond cubic**, and it is a **solid form of the element carbon**. Because of its **superior hardness and thermal conductivity **compared to other natural materials, diamond is **frequently employed in high-tech industrial products like cutting and polishing equipment**.
 
• **Coke is produced through the destructive distillation process of heating coal or oil without the presence of air**, resulting in a** grey, hard, and porous fuel with a high carbon content and minimal impurities**. When air pollution is a concern, it is also **utilised as a fuel** in stoves and forges and is a significant **industrial product**.
 
• The **brownish black sedimentary rock known as coal is combustible and is formed in rock strata known as coal seams**. Coal is **created when decomposing plant matter turns into peat** and is then **transformed into coal by the heat and pressure of deep burial **over the course of millions of years.
